title: Genotype-Phenotype Comparison in POGZ-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorders by Using Clinical Scoring

reviewer.method: Personally read the full 371-line main text, all four figures in original pixels and captions, all four complete tables including nine wrapped table pages, and every nonempty cell/blank convention/formula/cached value in all six supplementary workbook sheets. Read workbook structure, original font/fill/number-format groups and every merged range; additionally inspected all four full colored Sheet D pages. Corrected the Table 2 reading derivative header alignment and personally re-read its full corrected page. Full original title/PMID/DOI identity checked. Personally read both assigned selected packets in full, every allele and all 173 phenotype assertions; there are no assigned alternates. Prior acquisition/preparation is not personal reading. This new review spans the disk-full interruption; no canonical record was written until storage recovered. No target-case outcome files consulted.

audit.exposure_note: Required HANDOFF reading exposed aggregate history and a historical public-control HG002/FGFR2 case-specific rank. No target-case inference ranks, inference-output files or benchmark outcome summaries consulted. This review is not blinded.

phase.statement: Packet contains one variant in an autosomal dominant POGZ disorder. No second allele requires cis/trans resolution; this does not establish independently measured allele balance or parentage.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors classify L02 variant Pathogenic using PVS1/PM2/PM6/PP3 and attribute the phenotype to POGZ-related White-Sutton syndrome. L02 score31/severity4 and predicted escape from NMD are reported; no L02 RNA/protein experiment establishes that prediction or gain-of-function.

limitations: Main Table3 versus Sheet A cumulative-score discrepancies: L01 53 versus51; G01 9 versus10; W01 16 versus20; S01 13 versus12. Severity categories remain the same; L02 31 and R01 22 agree. No silent score correction.

NMD summaries are internally inconsistent: Sheet D F37 labels missense D01 as NMD yes, whereas Sheet E row70 states all missense escape NMD. Sheet E rows11/12 give42/67, whereas rows63/64 give46/63. C63 averages D!E2:E45 and E117:E118, encompassing non-NMD entries and omitting NL01 row116; C64 averages E46:E107, whose text 1? entries are not numeric. Main prose describes42 truncating NMD cases plus3 deletions. No reconciliation or fresh NMD mechanistic inference claimed.

The source uses different severity cutoffs by ascertainment/detail cohort. Less-detailed cohort has many blank/not-reported cells, with category totals sometimes zero; these are not clinical negative observations. Sheet C uncertain scores 1? and infant US02 reassignment are retained.

Sheet F uses broad48-person denominators (20 males/26 females/2 unreported sex) for many symptoms despite missing per-person information. B70 cardiovascular aggregate1 versus rows71-73 component counts3/2/3 also requires caution. Frequency totals are author calculations, not independently validated prevalence.

Hypothesized dominant-negative/gain-of-function versus haploinsufficiency and NMD grouping are not individual functional proof. Retrospective literature ascertainment, post hoc regional cutoffs, unequal detail and multiple comparisons constrain severity prediction. No wet-lab design/execution.

Figure4 is the paper's published facial-analysis comparison (48 affected photos, 21mild/27severe;79 controls), not a target benchmark outcome. Mild-versus-severe AUC0.74, p0.067 does not establish validated individual severity classification; published comparisons to controls do not substitute external clinical validation.

Whole-source review includes all13 present patients and all104 literature columns/rows. G01/G02 are related mother/child, US02 previously published; independent-case or family counts must not be inferred simply from117 entries. Other diagnoses/variants in S01/US01 and source uncertainty remain visible.
